label: GPT-6 Astra
output:
To: board:vendor-reviews
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Harbor Point Steno Service, Towson — Aria 3 recalibration and repair

Last month I told Dana I would write up Harbor Point after I had my writer back and had taken it through a real trial. It has now been through eight days of a civil trial, so here is the promised review.

I took my Stenvale Aria 3 to Harbor Point Steno Service on Monday, October 19, and picked it up Tuesday, October 27. That was six business days against the ten quoted. They are a two-person shop off York Road in Towson, with free parking in back.

The original estimate was $285 for a full recalibration, number bar sensor inspection, cleaning and firmware update. The completed work included a full keyboard recalibration, replacement of the number bar depression sensor, internal cleaning and an update from firmware 4.0.7 to 4.2.1. Gloria also found that the internal battery was holding about 60% of its rated capacity. She quoted $25 for replacement, parts and labor, and waited for my approval before doing it.

The final bill was $310, paid by card at pickup. I paid for it myself, as I do all my equipment; there was no reimbursement from the court. I think $310 was fair for what was done. Asking before adding the battery matters to me, even at that price. The work carries a 90-day warranty.

The important part: my first full day back was expert testimony from an engineer who talks in numbers. The number bar did not double a single stroke. After eight trial days, I am satisfied with the repair. The machine also came back with a printed, one-page service sheet listing every adjustment. I have never had that from anyone before, and I appreciated being able to see exactly what had been done.

They supplied a Stenvale Aria 2 loaner, so I was not left without a writer. That was useful, but the loaner was not trouble-free. Its tilt arm slipped mid-afternoon during a deposition, and I propped it on a legal pad for the rest of the day. I reported that to Gloria by email. When she notified me that my machine was ready, she acknowledged the problem and said they would repair the tilt arm. I cannot say whether that repair has since been completed.

The phone is the real weakness. Their stated phone hours are Tuesday through Thursday, 9 to 4 only. I called Wednesday, October 21, to ask about progress, and the phone rang out with no voicemail box set up. Gloria emailed the following day about the battery, so there was communication, but that does not make the phone arrangement adequate. For anyone working a Monday docket, those hours are a practical problem. Even within the stated hours, my call went unanswered and I could not leave a message.

Dana, based on this visit, I would trust Gloria with my Aria again, including for the number bar problem you described. The work was good, the turnaround beat the estimate, and the final price was explained and approved. I would arrange the timing and loaner in advance, check the loaner’s stand before leaving, and not count on reaching someone by phone when a working day goes wrong. Good repair work deserves credit; the phone coverage still needs improvement.

Maureen
